title: Reverse Nodes in k-Group
statement_short: Given the head of a linked list and a positive integer k, reverse the nodes of the list k at a time, and return the modified list. If the number of nodes is not a multiple of k, left-over nodes at the end should remain as they are.
hint: Node count up to 5000 requires O(n) time, reversing sub-lists of size k in-place with O(1) space.
why_not: Right: Two Pointers (or iterative pointer manipulation) checks if k nodes exist and reverses each k-group in-place in O(n) time and O(1) space. Not Stack: Pushing each k-group onto a stack reverses node order but uses O(k) extra space per group. Not HashMap / Hash Set: Storing node references in a map uses unnecessary O(n) memory. Not 1D DP: Subproblem state memoization does not apply to sequential node pointer rewiring.
